text: Module four. What can be sponsored, what it costs, and the seedlings behind it.
Every species carries three names — English, Kiswahili and scientific — a category, and what has actually happened to trees of its kind.
Two of those names can be edited. The scientific one cannot: every tree planted as this species points at it, so a correction is a new species and a decision about those trees.
Withdrawing a species stops it being offered, and nothing else. Trees already in the ground are unaffected — a catalogue decision, not a botanical one.
A care plan is what Otesha actually does for the tree. Thirty-six months, watering every three days, full care — with a monthly price.
Every price carries the date it came into force, because a new price does not reprice what has already been sold.
Behind all of it, the nursery. A batch of seedlings reserves a range of tree identifiers when it is sown, before anything is in the ground.
Which is what lets a tag be printed and carried to site. A batch cannot be planted against its identifiers until they have been.
And this is where it surfaces. Eight species, filtered by what the tree is for.
With the care plan spelled out, and the carbon figure marked as the estimate it is.
Five pages. Nothing reaches this screen by accident.
